attribution.note: Marcus's own conclusion in his Substack post, drawn from MathArena's reported scores.

semantics.note: Adding 'at IMO problems' matches the context, which compares IMO 2025 scores. The named comparison set and the MathArena qualifier are kept.

contract.note: Reading 'much stronger' as a large score gap on the same IMO 2025 problems is the ordinary reading. It correctly does not require equal compute.

evidence.note: MathArena's report, dated before the post: the best named model was Gemini 2.5 Pro at 13/42 after best-of-32 selection. The others trailed.
OpenAI's own disclosure of 35/42, graded by three former medalists it engaged. Not official IMO grading, but the gap over 13 is large.
Contemporaneous news report: Deep Think scored 35 under official IMO grading. It also notes OpenAI's grading was not through the IMO.

reviews.rationale: Both systems reported 35/42 on IMO 2025. The best named MathArena model averaged 13, and the others scored lower. Deep Think's score is officially graded. OpenAI's is self-commissioned, but even a one-point drop leaves a large gap, and nothing in the packet overturns it. Evaluation procedures and compute differ, but the claim as read concerns the score gap.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of OpenAI's public statements in his post.

semantics.note: Observation about OpenAI's public communications as of the post date. The revision correctly frames it as stated plans, not internal ones.

contract.note: Reading 'months' as multiple months, and 'clear plans' as a concrete access route or schedule, is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: Wei's July 19 post calls the IMO model experimental and says no release at that capability level for several months. It gives no access schedule. As OpenAI's own statement, it is the direct object of the claim.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own announcement put off any release at that capability level for several months and gave no concrete release or experimentation plan for the IMO model. Both parts of Marcus's description hold as of July 22, 2025. Undisclosed private arrangements cannot be ruled out, but the claim concerns public statements.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: In the source, 'reflects a cultural difference' attaches mainly to the IMO conduct, with the science records as illustration. The draft also drops the DeepMind collaboration element. Still broadly faithful.

contract.note: 'On the same level' has no measure, and 'culture' is undefined. The result depends on how scientific impact is compared, which the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: Independent Nobel recognition and wide adoption of AlphaFold. Supports the DeepMind side only.
DeepMind's own account of its 2021 collaborations with mathematicians. Supports the collaboration element.
EPFL's account of the joint tokamak-control project. A further DeepMind scientific collaboration.
Independent researchers used GPT-4 for autonomous chemistry. Shows OpenAI technology has scientific use, but establishes no comparable impact.
Los Alamos reports collaboration with OpenAI and use of its models. These are activities, not established comparative impact.
OpenAI and Retro protein work, preliminary and unpublished as of the report. Not shown to be at AlphaFold's level.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes DeepMind's collaborations and AlphaFold's recognition. It does not give a broad comparison of OpenAI's scientific record, and the packet itself says so. The cultural inference is not substantiated. The comparative and cultural parts are left unsettled by the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful observation about OpenAI's contact with the IMO before its announcement.

contract.note: Reading 'very little' as limited contact, not zero contact, is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: OpenAI researcher Brown says OpenAI was not in touch with the IMO and that he spoke to one organizer before posting. An admission by the company itself.
Brown says the IMO emailed about a Lean version about two months earlier and OpenAI declined. Rules out zero contact but is consistent with very little.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own accounts describe one declined invitation and a single notice to one organizer before the post. Nothing shows substantive coordination. That fits 'very little' communication, and nothing in the packet shows extensive prior contact.
